clue.text: Herb, that potty boy

definitions.meaning: a sweet aromatic herb used with tomatoes
... Fawlty, the manic hotelier of the British sitcom Fawlty Towers, a famously potty (crazy) man

explanation.surface: Someone points at a herb and at a toddler on his potty.
explanation.walkthrough: Fawlty Towers is a 1970s British TV comedy whose hotel owner is forever losing his temper; 'potty' is British slang for mad.
explanation.definitionFit: The herb is the pesto plant, and the boy is the comedy hotelier whose first name it shares.

clue.text: Tight little island girl

parts.note: Britain is the tight little island of the old song, and its female figure with trident and shield is the girl

explanation.surface: A drunk young woman on a small island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tight' suggests drunk, but 'The Tight Little Island' is a song about Britain; the girl is its personification on old British coins.
explanation.definitionFit: The helmeted woman on old pennies personifies Britain.

clue.text: Sent round a Greek letter of dubious wisdom

indicators.note: round means the first word goes around the next pieces

parts.note: pi is a Greek letter

explanation.surface: Someone sends a Greek letter whose wisdom is questionable.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is mostly used ironically, for would-be wise.

clue.text: He's landed in Scotland

parts.note: landed means owning land: a Scottish landowner

explanation.surface: A traveller arriving in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Landed' suggests arriving, but it means owning an estate.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scots word for a landed proprietor, lord of an estate.

clue.text: Hopelessly reckless speed perhaps, and more speed

indicators.note: perhaps signals the word speed is only one possible arrangement of its letters

parts.note: rate means speed, as in a rate of knots

explanation.surface: A reckless driver keeps speeding up, faster and faster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges SPEED into DESPE; 'more speed' then adds RATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone desperate has lost hope and so acts without caution.

clue.text: Columbia a little girl found over-exacting

indicators.note: in a down clue over means placed on top, so the girl comes above

parts.note: Di is a short girl's name, from Diana
strict means exacting

explanation.surface: A girl from Columbia is thought too demanding.
explanation.walkthrough: Columbia stands for the District of Columbia, Washington DC.
explanation.definitionFit: Washington DC is the District of Columbia, so the definition gives the word paired with it.

clue.text: Upsets the seasick medicine ?

definitions.meaning: read as ..., the pills for sea-sickness

explanation.surface: A patient knocks over his seasickness remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes S for sea before pills.
explanation.definitionFit: Upsetting a cup spills it, and seasickness tablets are pills, here prefixed S.

clue.text: What's extraordinarily special about the work of a bishop ?

indicators.note: about means the rearranged word goes around the work
extraordinarily suggests the word special appears in an unusual arrangement

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Someone asks what is so special about a bishop's job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extraordinarily' rearranges SPECIAL; that goes 'about' OP.
explanation.definitionFit: Episcopal means relating to bishops.

clue.text: Permanent living

explanation.surface: A permanent place to live.
explanation.definitionFit: An abiding love is lasting; to abide somewhere is to dwell there.

clue.text: The betrothed of Scott's " dastard in war "

definitions.text: The betrothed of Scott's " dastard in war "

parts.words: The betrothed of Scott's " dastard in war "
parts.note: in Walter Scott's ballad Lochinvar, a laggard in love and dastard in war was to wed the fair lady carried off by Lochinvar

explanation.surface: A literary question about a cowardly suitor in Scott.
explanation.walkthrough: In Scott's poem 'Lochinvar' the bride is snatched from her wedding to a coward.
explanation.definitionFit: She is the fair bride of Scott's ballad, promised to the cowardly laggard.

clue.text: Suggests that one politician is careless with the truth

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
an MP is a Member of Parliament
someone who lies is careless with the truth

explanation.surface: An insinuation that a certain politician is dishonest.
explanation.definitionFit: To hint at something without stating it is to suggest it.

clue.text: What's in a name for a start?

definitions.text: What's in a name for a start?

parts.words: What's in a name for a start
parts.note: the first letter of a name, the one that starts it off, as on a monogram

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean musing on names, asking where they begin.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface echoes Juliet's 'What's in a name?'; the answer is the letter at the start of a name.
explanation.definitionFit: The opening letter of a name is its first, starting letter.

clue.text: Dread a couple of points

parts.note: W and E are two compass points, west and east

explanation.surface: Fear of a couple of sharp points.
explanation.definitionFit: Awe is reverent fear, a kind of dread.

clue.text: Neglecting an abandoned particle

parts.note: derelict means abandoned, as a ruined house
an ion is a charged particle

explanation.surface: A scientist neglects a particle left lying around.
explanation.definitionFit: Dereliction of duty is neglect of it.

clue.text: Head brood bird

parts.note: nut is slang for the head
a hatch is a brood of chicks

explanation.surface: Three words that read like a farmyard note about a head of poultry.
explanation.definitionFit: A small tree-climbing songbird of Europe and America.

clue.text: Straying wild bear hurried to church

indicators.note: wild means the word bear runs out of control into a new order

parts.note: ran means hurried
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A wild bear wanders off and dashes to a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' rearranges BEAR into ABER.
explanation.definitionFit: Aberrance is a departure from the right course, a straying.

clue.text: Drunken type without what he makes of himself in the tap

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the drunken type surrounds the other piece

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drunkard
a drunk makes a pig of himself

explanation.surface: A drunkard sitting in a pub tap-room, making a pig of himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' means outside here, not lacking. The 'tap' of the surface is a pub's tap-room; the definition is a tap on a barrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A spigot is a peg or tap for drawing liquid from a cask.

clue.text: Not up to the game in Kent

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: Someone in Kent is not up to playing a game.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in south-east England, and Tonbridge a town there; 'up' turns NOT into TON.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonbridge is a town in the county of Kent.

clue.text: At a stretch it's unlike Mercy

definitions.meaning: Portia says the quality of mercy is not this, in The Merchant of Venice

explanation.surface: A remark that mercy is never forced.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's 'The quality of mercy is not strained' supplies the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A rope at full stretch is taut; Portia says mercy is not forced.

clue.text: Please change it to "Do not disturb "

indicators.note: change tells us to alter the order of the letters in the word please

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a hotel door sign to be reworded more politely.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleeping person should not be disturbed, as a hotel door sign says.

clue.text: Leslie swallows one drink ? An understatement

indicators.note: swallows means the short name takes the others inside it

parts.note: Les is short for Leslie
one is the Roman numeral I
a tot is a small drink

explanation.surface: Saying Leslie downed just one drink is putting it mildly.
explanation.definitionFit: Litotes is understatement by negation, like 'not bad'.

clue.text: Involved last animal begetting another

indicators.note: involved means twisted up, so the letters of the word last are tangled

parts.note: a lion is an animal

explanation.surface: A complicated chain of breeding animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Involved' rearranges LAST into STAL; LION follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A stud horse is kept to sire foals, begetting more horses.

clue.text: Push ? I'm beat

parts.note: a pulse is a beat

explanation.surface: Someone too exhausted to push any further.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beat' looks like tired; it is the heartbeat.
explanation.definitionFit: An impulse is a push or driving force.

clue.text: One gets pickled from being thus employed

parts.note: so means thus
used means employed

explanation.surface: A worker gets drunk because of his job.
explanation.definitionFit: Soused means pickled in brine, and also drunk.

clue.text: Discourage one having to speak on how' things get worse

parts.note: to deter is to discourage
one is the Roman numeral I
to orate is to speak formally

explanation.surface: Someone is put off from giving a speech about decline.
explanation.definitionFit: To decline in quality is to get worse.

clue.text: They may form stone or wear it away

definitions.text: They may form stone or wear it away

parts.words: They may form stone or wear it away
parts.note: falling water leaves limestone as stalactites, and constant falling water erodes rock

explanation.surface: A riddle about forces that build or erode rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Falling drops of water build stalactites and also hollow out stone.

clue.text: Fast kind of goose.?

definitions.meaning: the ... days are church fast days
the ... goose is the great northern diver

explanation.surface: A goose that is quick on its feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' is fasting, not speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Ember days are seasonal church fasts, and the ember goose is an old name for the great northern diver.

clue.text: If. issue lost, person still gets through

indicators.note: lost tells us the issue goes missing from the following word

parts.note: a son is issue, offspring

explanation.surface: A legal point: even without offspring, a person still inherits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' means children in wills; removing SON from PERSON leaves the Latin preposition.
explanation.definitionFit: Per means by way of, as in 'per post'.

clue.text: The time and my are savage-wild " (R & J)

definitions.text: The time and my are savage-wild

parts.words: The time and my are savage-wild
parts.note: a line from Romeo and Juliet with a word missing after my: Romeo's purposes are fierce

explanation.surface: A Shakespeare quotation with a blank to fill.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed clue has a dash after 'my'; Romeo says this at the Capulet tomb in Act 5 of Romeo and Juliet.
explanation.definitionFit: Romeo's line speaks of his purposes, the missing word being a plural of purpose.

clue.text: Jack's did after his downfall when tampered with?

definitions.text: Jack's did after his downfall when tampered with?

parts.words: Jack's did after his downfall when tampered with
parts.note: in the rhyme Jack fell down and broke his crown; the whole also means interfered with

explanation.surface: Jack and Jill, read as a tale of tampering.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as NOB BLED: nob is slang for head, and Jack's head bled after his fall. As one word it means tampered with, as a racehorse is drugged.
explanation.definitionFit: To nobble a horse or juror is to interfere with it illicitly.

clue.text: Old Bob's in drink, finished and hanged

indicators.note: in places the bob inside the drink

parts.note: to sup is to drink
a bob was the old British shilling, abbreviated s
ended means finished

explanation.surface: A man called Bob drank, came to an end and was hanged.
explanation.walkthrough: Bob is British slang for a shilling, a pre-1971 coin, whose abbreviation is s.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanging something up suspends it.

clue.text: Secure the bird

definitions.meaning: to fasten a rope by threading it through a ring or block
the female of the ruff, a wading bird

explanation.surface: Instructions to catch and keep a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors thread a rope to fasten it, and the female ruff has its own name, the same word.
